svg.text: MAKING THINGS STERILE — AND KEEPING THEM SO
Clean, disinfected and sterile are three different things. Only one kills spores.

g.text: Removes visible dirt
and most organisms.
Always comes first.
Kills most organisms
but not spores.
Surfaces, some scopes.
Kills everything,
including spores.
Anything entering tissue.
Pressure lets steam get hotter than boiling water, and it is the HEAT that kills, not the pressure.
Steam must reach every surface, so packs are never crammed in, and hollow items must be open.

svg.text: Boiling does not sterilise. It does not reach the temperature that destroys spores.
WHAT THE TAPE DOES AND DOES NOT TELL YOU

g.text: Colour change on the tape means the
pack was PROCESSED.
It does not prove the contents are
sterile. Only the biological indicator does.
It is torn, damp, or has been wet
It is past its expiry date
It has been dropped on the floor
You are not sure. Doubt means discard.

svg.text: MOISTURE TRAVELS, SO WET IS THE SAME AS DIRTY

g.text: A damp drape wicks organisms straight through from the unsterile surface beneath it. This is why a wet

svg.text: field is contaminated even when nothing visibly touched it.
Sterile touches only sterile. Below waist level, behind your back, and out of sight are all unsterile.
